name: Sicilian Defense
description: A fighting Black course that teaches the main c5 response first, then how to meet simple White setups.

branches.title: Main Line: c5 Against e4

moves.title: White claims center
moves.explanation: White controls d5 and f5. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Sicilian creates imbalance: Black trades the c-pawn for central influence and develops before counterattacking.

moves.title: Attack d4
moves.explanation: c5 challenges the center from the side and creates an imbalanced game. c5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Sicilian creates imbalance: Black trades the c-pawn for central influence and develops before counterattacking.

moves.title: Develop to f3
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops a knight to f3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d4
moves.explanation: cxd4 shows how trades enter the opening. This is an equal trade. Equal trades are good when they improve your structure, open a file, or remove an active enemy piece. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d4
moves.explanation: Nxd4 shows how trades enter the opening. This capture should only be played because it gains time, opens lines, or solves a concrete problem. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Improve with a6
moves.explanation: a6 is a practical improving move for Black. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: Develop to e2
moves.explanation: Be2 improves a piece and adds control over important squares. Developed pieces create threats naturally, so you do not need to force an attack before castling.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: The Sicilian creates imbalance: Black trades the c-pawn for central influence and develops before counterattacking.
Good trades usually remove an active enemy piece, open a useful file, or simplify once your king is safe.
After the opening, do not drift: improve your worst piece, connect rooks, and look for one clear pawn break.

ideas: The Sicilian creates imbalance: Black trades the c-pawn for central influence and develops before counterattacking.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Opening the game without king safety.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
